18.1.5.6 Reduction of Carboxylic Acids and Esters

Carboxylic acids are exceedingly difficult to reduce. A very powerful reducing agent such as lithium aluminium hydride is required to convert a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol. Sodium borohydride is not a potent hydride donor as lithium aluminium hydride and does not reduce carboxylic acids.

Esters can also be reduced by lithium aluminium hydride. Two alcohols are formed from each ester molecule. The acyl group of the ester is cleaved, giving a primary alcohol.

Tidbit

Lithium aluminium hydride and sodium borohydride are hydride (H⁻) donors. Lithium aluminium hydride is much stronger reducing agent than sodium borohydride.

18.1.6 Reactivity

The functional group of the alcohols is the hydroxyl group, which is the reactive site. This group has two reactive covalent bonds, the C–O bond and the O–H bond. The electronegativity of oxygen is substantially greater than that of carbon and hydrogen. Consequently, the covalent bonds of this functional group are polarized so that oxygen is electron rich and both carbon and hydrogen are electrophilic. The oxygen atom of alcohols has two unshared pairs of electrons and hence is an electron rich centre.

Alcohols are reactive compounds. They readily react with polar or ionic reagents. Generally, the reactions of alcohol involve the fission of either the O–H bond or the C–O bond. The common reactions of alcohols are substitution, elimination and oxidation reactions.

18.1.7 Reactions of Alcohols

18.1.7.1 Reaction with Halogen acids (HX) to give Alkyl halides

Alcohols react with halogen acids to form alkyl halides by replacement of hydroxyl group with halogen atom (Section 17.1.4.1).

Reactivity of halogen acid increases with acid strength. In case hydrogen chloride, anhydrous zinc chloride is used as catalyst while treating alcohol to produce alkyl chlorides.

الکوحلز کا فعلی گروپ ہائیڈروآکسل گروپ ہے، جو تعامل کا مقام ہے۔ اس گروپ میں دو تعامل پذیر شریک گرفتی بند ہیں، C–O بند اور O–H بند۔ آکسیجن کی برقی منفیت کاربن اور ہائیڈروجن سے کافی زیادہ ہے۔ نتیجتاً اس فعلی گروپ کے شریک گرفتی بند اس طرح قطبی ہوتے ہیں کہ آکسیجن الیکٹرانوں سے بھرپور اور کاربن اور ہائیڈروجن دونوں الیکٹروفائلی ہوتے ہیں۔ الکوحلز کے آکسیجن ایٹم پر الیکٹرانوں کے دو غیر مشترک جوڑے ہوتے ہیں اور اس لیے یہ الیکٹرانوں سے بھرپور مرکز ہے۔

الکوحلز تعامل پذیر مرکبات ہیں۔ یہ قطبی یا آئنی عاملوں سے آسانی سے تعامل کرتے ہیں۔ عموماً الکوحل کے تعاملات میں یا تو O–H بند یا C–O بند ٹوٹتا ہے۔ الکوحلز کے عام تعاملات تبادلہ، اخراج اور تکسید کے تعاملات ہیں۔

18.1.7 الکوحلز کے تعاملات

18.1.7.1 ہیلوجن تیزابوں (HX) سے تعامل کر کے الکائل ہیلائیڈز بنانا

الکوحلز ہیلوجن تیزابوں سے تعامل کر کے ہائیڈروآکسل گروپ کو ہیلوجن ایٹم سے بدل کر الکائل ہیلائیڈز بناتے ہیں (حصہ 17.1.4.1)۔

ہیلوجن تیزاب کی تعامل پذیری تیزاب کی طاقت کے ساتھ بڑھتی ہے۔ ہائیڈروجن کلورائیڈ کی صورت میں الکوحل سے الکائل کلورائیڈز بنانے کے لیے بے آب زنک کلورائیڈ بطور عمل انگیز استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

18.1.5.6 Reduction of Carboxylic Acids and Esters

Carboxylic acids are exceedingly difficult to reduce. A very powerful reducing agent such as lithium aluminium hydride is required to convert a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol. Sodium borohydride is not a potent hydride donor as lithium aluminium hydride and does not reduce carboxylic acids.

Esters can also be reduced by lithium aluminium hydride. Two alcohols are formed from each ester molecule. The acyl group of the ester is cleaved, giving a primary alcohol.

Tidbit

Lithium aluminium hydride and sodium borohydride are hydride (H⁻) donors. Lithium aluminium hydride is much stronger reducing agent than sodium borohydride.

18.1.6 Reactivity

The functional group of the alcohols is the hydroxyl group, which is the reactive site. This group has two reactive covalent bonds, the C–O bond and the O–H bond. The electronegativity of oxygen is substantially greater than that of carbon and hydrogen. Consequently, the covalent bonds of this functional group are polarized so that oxygen is electron rich and both carbon and hydrogen are electrophilic. The oxygen atom of alcohols has two unshared pairs of electrons and hence is an electron rich centre.

Alcohols are reactive compounds. They readily react with polar or ionic reagents. Generally, the reactions of alcohol involve the fission of either the O–H bond or the C–O bond. The common reactions of alcohols are substitution, elimination and oxidation reactions.

18.1.7 Reactions of Alcohols

18.1.7.1 Reaction with Halogen acids (HX) to give Alkyl halides

Alcohols react with halogen acids to form alkyl halides by replacement of hydroxyl group with halogen atom (Section 17.1.4.1).

Reactivity of halogen acid increases with acid strength. In case hydrogen chloride, anhydrous zinc chloride is used as catalyst while treating alcohol to produce alkyl chlorides.
